sources.entry: Hangar - Runs AI coding agents in macOS, Linux or Windows virtual machines, with allow-listed network access and snapshots. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/baseguard/hangar) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Hangar
summary.one_liner: Hangar is a free, open-source Mac app and command line for running AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex inside macOS, Linux or Windows virtual machines with allow-listed network access and snapshots.
summary.category: macos vm sandbox for ai agents
use_cases: Running Claude Code or Codex without giving them access to your files
Restricting which websites an AI agent can reach
Undoing changes an agent made by restoring a snapshot
Running several agent VMs in parallel from one snapshot
Testing software in disposable macOS, Linux or Windows VMs
summary.what_it_does: Hangar creates and runs virtual machines on Apple silicon Macs, with macOS, Linux (Debian and Ubuntu images or custom ISOs) and Windows 11 Arm guests. A window shows every VM's screen, resource use and network connections, and the hangar command line manages the same VMs. An optional allow list limits which sites a VM can reach, and Hangar logs lookups, connections and data volume from outside the VM. API keys are stored in the Mac Keychain and swapped in for a placeholder value on requests to chosen sites. Snapshots save a VM's disk instantly and can be restored to discard later changes, and copies can be made from a snapshot to run several VMs. The hangar mcp server lets Claude Code or Codex create, start and snapshot VMs, though it cannot delete them.
notable: Allow-listed network access and connection logging enforced from outside the VM
API keys stay in macOS Keychain; VM only sees a fake value replaced on outbound requests
Snapshots plus MCP server so Claude Code or Codex can manage VMs
caveats: Requires macOS 27 or later and an Apple silicon Mac
The agent cannot delete VMs through the MCP server
Windows 11 support is limited to Microsoft's Arm ISO
